title: this binding: default, implicit, explicit, and arrow functions
hook: In JavaScript, this is not the object where a function was written — it is the object chosen when the function is called. FAANG interviews love the binding matrix because one wrong assumption breaks React handlers, class methods, and callbacks.

blocks.text: **this** is a runtime binding set by the **call site** (except arrow functions and bound functions). The five rules: **default** (strict: undefined), **implicit** (`obj.method()` → this is obj), **explicit** (`call/apply/bind`), **new** (`new Fn()` → fresh object), and **arrow** (lexical this from enclosing scope).

entries.plainDefinition: Where a function is invoked — determines this.
Method call sets this to the receiver object.
Forcing this with call, apply, or bind.
Arrow functions capture this from enclosing scope.

blocks.text: Lost **this** is the top bug in event handlers and callbacks: `addEventListener('click', obj.handleClick)` passes the function without the object. C# instance methods carry **this** implicitly and cannot detach the same way.

blocks.title: Priority when rules compete
blocks.body: new beats bind beats implicit beats default. Arrows ignore call-site rules.

snippet.label: Default versus implicit
snippet.explanation: Method call binds obj; extracted function uses default binding.

snippet.label: call, apply, bind
snippet.explanation: call sets this for one call; bind returns function with fixed this.

snippet.label: Class method versus arrow field
snippet.explanation: Prototype method loses this when detached; arrow field captures instance this.

snippet.label: Interview trace — setTimeout in method
snippet.explanation: Ordinary callback loses this; arrow captures getXLater's this (obj).

blocks.title: Passing class method as callback
blocks.body: `setTimeout(this.tick, 1000)` loses this — use arrow, bind, or wrapper.

blocks.text: Soft bind and currying reuse explicit binding. React class autobinding existed because of implicit loss. bind allocates a wrapper — hot paths may use arrow fields consciously. Interview tracing: determine this from call shape only.

snippet.label: Failure mode — event handler
snippet.explanation: Passing method reference loses implicit binding — use bind or arrow field.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying this is always the defining object. Forgetting strict default is undefined. Claiming bind and call are identical.

interviewTakeaways: this is set by call site: default, implicit, explicit, new, or lexical (arrow).
Detaching a method loses implicit binding.
Arrow functions inherit enclosing this; class field arrows fix callbacks.
60s: Five rules — new > bind > implicit > default; arrows lexical. obj.method() binds obj; callback loses it. Fix with bind, arrow field, or wrapper.
Follow-up: predict this in setTimeout with function versus arrow inside a method.
commonPitfalls: Weak: 'this is the function owner.' Strong: this chosen at invocation.
Passing obj.handle as event listener without bind.
Arrow as prototype method expecting instance this.

jsTsCorrelations.note: C# instance methods always receive the instance — no detached-method trap.
TS types this on functions but does not change runtime binding.
